MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N270unmasked layer
This neuron fires weakly on the token that opens a new clause/sentence immediately after a period or comma — often the first (capitalized) sub-word piece of the new word ("This", "U" in "Ugh", "C" in "Cures") — or on a function word completing a formulaic phrase ("coming up with", "cute and cuddly"); mid-sentence conjunctions/prepositions and hyphens ("are", "and", "at", "-") strongly suppress it.

L29·N8355unmasked layer
This neuron activates on the token immediately preceding an indefinite article "a"/"A" (e.g. "check **on** a variety", "**including** a", "Design **Lovely** A", "**us** for/a quote", "?\n" before "A:"), and is strongly suppressed when that pre-"a" token is part of a fixed idiomatic collocation ("once **upon** a time", "work up... **of** a sweat", "one **of** a kind", "seven **days** a week") — i.e. it marks the slot before a free/ordinary "a" rather than a memorized multiword phrase.

This neuron has no coherent semantic trigger — it fires weakly and idiosyncratically on assorted mid-phrase tokens (the determiner "this", sub-word pieces like "che"/"La", the colon in a time, a sentence-final ".\n"), and is most strongly *suppressed* by single-capital-letter initials in name/citation strings (e.g. "D.", "T.B."), so it looks like a noisy/polysemantic unit whose clearest signal is negative on abbreviation initials.
